shortDescription: Adds or removes a user from a MongoDB database

options.name: atlas_auth
options.description: Authentication path intended for MongoDB Atlas Instances

options.name: auth_mechanism
options.description: Authentication type.

options.name: authentication_restrictions
options.description:
The authentication restrictions the server enforces on the user. Specifies a list of IP addresses and CIDR ranges the user is allowed to connect from and/or server addresses they can connect to. Provide a list of dictionaries with the following fields: C(clientSource) (list) and C(serverAddress) (list).
 Provide an empty list if you don't want to use the field.

options.name: connection_options
options.description: Additional connection options. Supply as a list of dicts or strings containing key value pairs seperated with '='.

options.name: create_for_localhost_exception
options.description: This is parmeter is only useful for handling special treatment around the localhost exception. If C(login_user) is defined, then the localhost exception is not active and this parameter has no effect. If this file is NOT present (and C(login_user) is not defined), then touch this file after successfully adding the user. If this file is present (and C(login_user) is not defined), then skip this task.

options.name: database
options.description: The name of the database to add/remove the user from.

options.name: login_database
options.description: The database where login credentials are stored.

options.name: login_host
options.description: The host running MongoDB instance to login to.

options.name: login_password
options.description: The password used to authenticate with. Required when I(login_user) is specified.

options.name: login_port
options.description: The MongoDB server port to login to.

options.name: login_user
options.description: The MongoDB user to login with. Required when I(login_password) is specified.

options.name: name
options.description: The name of the user to add or remove.

options.name: password
options.description: The password to use for the user.

options.name: replica_set
options.description: Replica set to connect to (automatically connects to primary for writes). Leave empty if you need the localhost exception, e.g. to create the initial user

options.name: roles
options.description:
The database user roles valid values could either be one or more of the following strings: 'read', 'readWrite', 'dbAdmin', 'userAdmin', 'clusterAdmin', 'readAnyDatabase', 'readWriteAnyDatabase', 'userAdminAnyDatabase', 'dbAdminAnyDatabase'
 Or the following dictionary '{ db: DATABASE_NAME, role: ROLE_NAME }'. This param requires pymongo 2.5+. If it is a string, mongodb 2.4+ is also required. If it is a dictionary, mongo 2.6+ is required.

options.name: ssl
options.description: Whether to use an SSL connection when connecting to the database.

options.name: ssl_ca_certs
options.description: The ssl_ca_certs option takes a path to a CA file.

options.name: ssl_cert_reqs
options.description: Specifies whether a certificate is required from the other side of the connection, and whether it will be validated if provided.

options.name: ssl_certfile
options.description: Present a client certificate using the ssl_certfile option.

options.name: ssl_crlfile
options.description: The ssl_crlfile option takes a path to a CRL file.

options.name: ssl_keyfile
options.description: Private key for the client certificate.

options.name: ssl_pem_passphrase
options.description: Passphrase to decrypt encrypted private keys.

options.name: state
options.description: The database user state.

options.name: strict_compatibility
options.description: Enforce strict requirements for pymongo and MongoDB software versions

options.name: update_password
options.description: C(always) will always update passwords and cause the module to return changed. C(on_create) will only set the password for newly created users. This must be C(always) to use the localhost exception when adding the first admin user. This option is effectively ignored when using x.509 certs. It is defaulted to 'on_create' to maintain a           a specific module behaviour when the login_database is '$external'.
